title: Sourcing playbook orientation and legal queue review
summary: Intro to Redwood onboarding playbook focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiering, and pricing approval path. Security asked for KMS and SOC2 artifacts; legal requested specific indemnity language options. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share MSA/DPA draft, SE to provide topology and private VPC checklist, and schedule a KMS deep-dive next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Simmons (Pinecrest Procurement), Ravi Gupta (Pinecrest Security), Emma Torres (Pinecrest Legal), Tom Blake (Pinecrest Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Orientation on sourcing playbook, review of legal queue items (MSA/DPA), SLA asks, and next steps for procurement escalation.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. This is Maya from Redwood, with Jonah — hey Jonah.
[00:06] Jonah: Hey all, thanks.
[00:08] Laura: Hi, Laura here. We have most of the procurement and legal folks on.
[00:12] Ravi: Ravi, security. Quick FYI: I'll flag the KMS requirements early.
[00:15] Emma: Emma, legal. We'll be focused on the MSA and data controls.
[00:18] Tom: Tom, engineering. I'll listen for VPC and onboarding bits.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Goal for today is quick orientation to our sourcing playbook and to triage the items in your legal queue so we can get you to an approval decision faster. We'll cover MSA redline approach, DPA specifics, SLA tiers, and the pricing approval timeline.
[00:34] Laura: Sound good. Procurement is mostly timeline driven — we have a monthly committee meeting on Sep 15, so anything before that helps.
[00:40] Maya: Perfect, that gives us a target. Jonah, do you want to run the high-level onboarding steps?
[00:46] Jonah: Sure. So typical Redwood flow — we have three tracks: hosted API (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment for VPC/on-prem. For enterprise customers with PHI-ish data we generally recommend private or dedicated depending on throughput. There was a note in the intake about egress and residency, can you expand Laura?
[01:05] Laura: Yes. Pinecrest requires US-data residency for patient-adjacent datasets. We also have a clause requiring log retention to our SIEM for 90 days.
[01:13] Jonah: Okay, we can support region restrictions and syslog forwarding. On the private deployment we can integrate with customer KMS, or for dedicated we offer support for envelope encryption.
[01:23] Ravi: When you say integrate with KMS, is that customer-managed keys in HSM, or just a reference?
[01:27] Jonah: We support both. For private deployments you can bring your KMS/HSM and we integrate via standard APIs — we'll share the key flow diagram. For hosted, we offer Redwood-managed keys but with customer-managed key options for enterprise (we call it Bring-Your-Own-Key).
[01:40] Ravi: Good. Need to see architecture and control points, and proof of SOC2.
[01:45] Emma: On the legal side, we saw the MSA boilerplate but there are three specific redline asks: indemnity cap clarification, data breach notification timing (24 vs 72 hours), and subprocessor disclosure cadence.
[01:58] Maya: Got it. Our typical position is 72 hours for initial notification followed by updates, but we can be flexible depending on materiality. For indemnity, we have a standard cap tied to fees but we're open to discussing carve-outs for gross negligence.
[02:12] Emma: Can you share the exact language options? We want to present a clean compare view to our counsel.
[02:16] Maya: Yes — we'll send a tracked redline and a clean copy.
[02:19] Laura: Also, pricing approvals — procurement needs a billing contact and cost estimate that includes surge/burst scenarios.
[02:26] Jonah: We'll include a sample cost sheet with per-token and per-hour reserved capacity numbers, plus a model for burst costs. We can also model a 6-month pilot to show usage.
[02:35] Tom: On onboarding, what's the rough time-to-prod for a private deployment? I'm thinking about network firewall exceptions and certs.
[02:41] Jonah: Typical private deployment preflight is 4-6 weeks, depending on network readiness and KMS cert provisioning. Dedicated can be faster — 2-3 weeks if we already have approved IP ranges and credentials. Edge cases extend that.
[02:53] Laura: That fits with our Sep 15 committee if we have the MSA by early week of Sep 6.
[02:58] Maya: Okay, target: MSA + DPA redline to you by Sep 3. Jonah will package topology and onboarding checklist by Sep 6.
[03:06] Emma: About the DPA: we need clarity on subprocessors and whether you will notify us for added subprocessors or have a list.
[03:13] Maya: We maintain a subprocessor list; for major changes we notify customers, and for critical subprocessors we'll seek prior consent in the DPA. We'll include that language in the draft.
[03:21] Ravi: What about data deletion and backups retention? Some of our policies require 30-day restore window and 90-day logs.
[03:28] Jonah: We can support configurable retention for generated content and logs. We'll detail retention policies and scrub procedures in the DPA attachment.
[03:35] Tom: Any special network egress costs we should plan for?
[03:38] Jonah: Egress fees depend on deployment — private on-prem has no provider egress; hosted has cloud egress which we can estimate. We'll include that in the cost model.
[03:45] Maya: Quick Q from procurement: do you have a usage SLA table?
[03:49] Jonah: Yes, our SLA tiers include 99.9% for standard, 99.95% for enterprise reserved with response time commitments. We'll send the SLA matrix. Note: SLA remedies are typically service credits.
[04:03] Emma: For SLA, we need clarity on measurement window and exclusions, especially force majeure and maintenance windows.
[04:09] Maya: We'll include exclusion language and a sample measurement approach in the redline.
[04:13] Laura: On approvals, our finance needs an approved price sheet and an agreed minimum commit for Dedicated. What are your typical commit models?
[04:21] Jonah: We offer monthly reserved pools with commit levels and burst options. Commit discounts tier down at 3mo, 6mo, and 12mo bands. We'll provide an example pricing schedule.
[04:33] Ravi: Security artifacts: can you publish pen-test reports and a SOC2 report?
[04:37] Maya: Yes, SOC2 Type II and pen-test summaries are available under NDA. We'll add a link to the security folder in the follow-up.
[04:45] Emma: We'll need to run this through our legal intake. Who's the Redwood contact for redlines?
[04:50] Maya: That will be me — I'll coordinate comments and feed them to our legal. Jonah will help with technical attachments.
[04:56] Tom: On the tech deep-dive, can we schedule a separate call to validate performance for our worst-case latency workloads? We're using 1k token prompts and expect sub-500ms p95 for inference.
[05:07] Jonah: Sub-500ms p95 is aggressive depending on model and instance class. For certain quantized models on dedicated GPUs we can get close, but we'll need to run an SLA benchmark. Suggest we run a scoped perf test — I'll propose a configuration matrix.
[05:20] Ravi: Please include KV cache behavior and warm/cold cache effects in the perf plan.
[05:25] Jonah: Will do.
[05:27] [05:27] Laura: Quick administrative Q — do you require a PO before MSA signature?
[05:30] Maya: We typically don't require a PO to sign the MSA; POs come later for billing. Procurement practices vary, so we'll adapt.
[05:36] Emma: Indemnity language — can you outline your standard cap? We need to present to counsel.
[05:40] Maya: Standard cap equals total fees paid in prior 12 months, with carve-outs for WILLFUL misconduct and IP infringement. We can propose language that tightens the scope if needed.
[05:50] Tom: On technical onboarding, what logs are shipped to customer SIEM? Is it audit-only or transcript-level?
[05:56] Jonah: By default we index metadata and access logs. Transcripts and payloads are considered sensitive; we can stream metadata and alerts to SIEM, and can set up selective streaming of non-sensitive logs with redaction. We'll document options.
[06:12] Laura: That will be important for our privacy team.
[06:15] Maya: I'm going to call out three paths in the playbook: 1) Quick hosted pilot (2 weeks), 2) Reserved Dedicated pilot (4-8 weeks), 3) Private deployment (4-12 weeks). Each path has a different legal and security checklist.
[06:29] Ravi: For private deployment, we need to validate vendor access controls and RBAC. Do you support SSO via SAML/SCIM?
[06:36] Jonah: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll share SSO integration docs.
[06:42] Emma: On subprocessors again — can you provide a list of subprocessor categories and a snapshot of current providers? Even if redacted, a category list helps.
[06:52] Maya: Yes. We'll provide a subprocessor snapshot and a cadence for updates.
[06:56] [07:00] Laura: Let's talk timeline: If Redwood sends redlines and the pricing sheet by Sep 3, procurement meets Sep 7 internally and the governance committee Sep 15. Then legal signoff by end of month ideally.
[07:11] Maya: That timeline sounds doable on our side.
[07:14] Jonah: I'll compile the technical artifacts: topology diagram (PDF), onboarding checklist (CSV), and perf test template (sheet).
[07:21] Ravi: We'll need to understand retention deletion APIs — is there a programmatic purge we can call?
[07:25] Jonah: Yes, delete APIs exist on private and dedicated; for hosted we offer deletion and retention controls via the console and APIs. We'll show sample curl snippets.
[07:33] Emma: Do you have any standing exceptions you won't take on in MSA? For example, unlimited liability or blanket data escrow requirements.
[07:41] Maya: We generally resist unlimited liability. Data escrow can be discussed for regulated customers but is not standard. We'll note these as negotiable with appropriate commercial terms.
[07:50] Laura: On the pricing approval, can you give a notional spend estimate for a 3-month pilot with 50k inference calls per month?
[07:57] Jonah: Rough for hosted generative text calls we can ballpark $X — I'll include a worked example in the cost model; it'll show token-based and reserved capacity comparisons.
[08:07] Tom: Please include examples for quantized vs fp16 model choices and expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
[08:12] Jonah: Yes, different model families and quantization change cost by up to 40%-60% depending on throughput.
[08:20] Ravi: On SOC2, can you confirm the scope? Is inference runtime included?
[08:25] Maya: SOC2 reports cover our control plane and runtime as defined in the attestation — we'll provide the scope statement.
[08:30] Emma: If you can get all artifacts in an NDA link, that speeds legal review.
[08:34] Maya: We'll put the artifacts in an NDA-protected folder and share link.
[08:38] [08:40] Laura: Ok I think we have enough to move the procurement intake. A couple of action items for Redwood?
[08:45] Maya: Yes — I'll recap at the end but high level: MSA/DPA draft by Sep 3, topology & onboarding checklist by Sep 6, security artifacts under NDA, pricing workbook with burst modeling.
[08:56] Emma: Also, provide specific redline options for notification timing and indemnity carve-outs.
[09:02] Jonah: On the technical side, we'll propose a perf test and include KV-cache notes and warmup strategies.
[09:09] Tom: Can we do a technical deep dive the week of Sep 6? Our infra lead has availability Wed morning (Sep 8).
[09:16] Jonah: I'll check calendars and propose slots.
[09:18] Laura: Anything else from legal or security?
[09:20] Ravi: One more: we require vulnerability scanning frequency and a disclosure SLA for critical CVEs.
[09:26] Maya: We'll include vulnerability scanning cadence and a disclosure window in the security pack.
[09:32] Emma: Regarding DPA, we'll need to ensure data deletion and access revocation map to our retention policies.
[09:38] Jonah: We'll provide mapping tables for data types and retention behaviors.
[09:42] [09:45] Maya: Great. Before we wrap, quick recap and next steps. I'll list them and then put them in email.
[09:52] Maya: 1) Redwood to send MSA + DPA draft (tracked redline and clean copy) by Sep 3. 2) Redwood SE (Jonah) to deliver topology diagram, onboarding checklist, and perf template by Sep 6. 3) Security pack (SOC2, pen-test summary) under NDA link by Sep 3. 4) Pricing workbook and reserve vs hosted cost modeling by Sep 3. 5) Schedule technical deep-dive (KMS/perf) for week of Sep 6 — propose Sep 8 Wed morning as candidate.
[10:20] Laura: That works for procurement and governance.
[10:22] Emma: Legal will review the redlines and come back with a consolidated mark no later than Sep 10.
[10:26] Ravi: Security will review artifacts and send required control list by Sep 4.
[10:30] Tom: Engineering will be on the tech deep-dive.
[10:33] Maya: Awesome. We'll follow up with an email that includes links to the artifacts. Any final questions?
[10:38] Laura: None here. Thanks.
[10:40] Maya: Thanks everyone, appreciate the time. We'll be in touch.

End of transcript.

Schedule KMS and performance deep-dive week of Sep 6 (SE-led)
